card.band: 8 h. The parser and binary protocol are quick. Compact-protocol varint/zigzag edge cases, JSON protocol quirks, union and default semantics, and error classification are the deep parts. A frontier agent reaches about 60 to 75 percent. A weaker model stops at the binary protocol.
card.cheat: Using a pip thrift package: not installable offline. Golden vectors are hidden and generated from unseen IDLs, so memorising samples fails.
card.grading: Hidden cases: (a) 1000+ IDL files taken from thrift's own test/ tree and generated variants, comparing a canonical AST dump and error class against the real compiler; (b) cross-language wire-byte tests, where the runtime must encode and decode structures byte-identical to golden vectors from the C++ library across the three protocols; (c) a service round-trip suite. Scored per bucket.
card.reference: The upstream compiler and Python library, trimmed to the required subset, are our reference. They pass the whole hidden set by construction.
card.task: /app ships a skeleton. The agent builds a Thrift IDL parser and validator (includes, typedefs, enums, unions, exceptions, services, annotations, constants). It adds a Python code generator plus a runtime for the binary, compact and JSON protocols and framed/buffered transports. A client-server pair runs over local sockets.

spike_plan.kill_if: Build fails or needs network; fewer than about 200 usable IDL files; output is nondeterministic; or the AST dump and error-class mapping cannot be specified for the grader.
spike_plan.pass_if: Compiler builds offline-reproducible from the tag in under 30 min; at least 150 IDL files classify deterministically; golden bytes are reproducible across runs and round-trip for all three protocols; total IDL count is verifiable at 1000+ or the bucket is rescoped.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone apache/thrift at tag v0.25.0 (no history needed beyond the tag).
Build the C++ compiler (cmake, bison, flex) and record wall time and any failures; this replaces the empty smoke_build.
Run the built thrift binary over the 32 direct .thrift files in test/ and the subdirectories; record exit code and first error line per file, and rerun twice to check determinism.
Count the real total of .thrift files under test/ via a full clone (not the truncated API listing) to settle the 1000+ IDL claim.

pip install thrift==0.22.0 in a venv (or build lib/py from the tag); write a fixed struct with nested list, map, union, and default-valued fields; encode with TBinaryProtocol, TCompactProtocol, TJSONProtocol and save bytes as golden vectors.
Rerun the encoder twice and diff bytes to confirm determinism; decode each vector back and compare to the input.
Draft the AST dump and error-class taxonomy on paper for 5 IDL files and check whether the real compiler output can be mapped to it; if not, the grading contract is underspecified.

v1.summary: The Apache Thrift v0.25.0 source is real, public and Apache-2.0 licensed, with a substantial compiler and Python runtime, but the seed's 1000+ IDL corpus claim is unverified (only 32 visible .thrift files directly under test/) and the AST dump format is undefined. As specified the scope is about 20h of work, so it fails K9 at the 8h tier and should be resubmitted at 20h or rescoped to a subset that fits 8h.
